clauses.clause: Explain concepts by interpreting texts.
clauses.note: Students interpret a read-aloud and videos to describe what people and animals do during day and night.

clauses.clause: Learn concepts by interpreting texts.
clauses.note: Students observe and discuss information from texts and videos to build understanding of day vs. night.

clauses.clause: Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.
clauses.note: Students discuss and sort pictures but do not create written or other constructed texts to show understanding.

verdicts.evidence:
Tell students that as they watch the videos, they should look carefully to see what they notice and observe about the sky, the sun, the moon, and what animals and people are doing during the daytime and during the nighttime. Tell students they should also think about the questions they have as they watch the videos.
Inform students that after they watch each video, they will have a chance to share their thinking with a partner using the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol. Remind them that they used this protocol in Module 1 and review as necessary using the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.)
Play 'City Street Time Lapse Stock Video.'
Guide students through the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol using this question:
'What is one thing you noticed about what people and animals do during the day?'
Provide a sentence frame if necessary:
-'I noticed that during the day, people and animals __________.'
verdicts.rationale: Students interpret and discuss information from a book and videos to explain and learn about day and night, but they do not construct texts to demonstrate their understanding. [REJECTED: evidence missing or not found in lesson raw text]
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote NOT found in lesson raw text (possible fabrication)
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Explain and learn concepts and processes by interpreting and constructing texts. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Explore digital sources of information.

clauses.clause: Explore personal communication as a source of information.
clauses.note: Students discuss and share observations with peers and teacher.

clauses.clause: Identify different modes of communication: print, digital, auditory, and visual.

clauses.clause: Identify techniques used to craft stories, including characters, setting, major events, and dialogue.
clauses.note: Students identify the setting (day vs. night) and events/actions in the text; they discuss what the sun/moon see.

clauses.clause: Identify a simple plot with a problem and solution.
clauses.note: No task asks students to find a problem and solution or outline a plot.

clauses.clause: Describe traits of the main characters and explain how their words and actions support the central message, lesson, or moral of the story.
clauses.note: Students do not analyze character traits or connect actions/words to a central message.

clauses.clause: With adult support, compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories across diverse cultures.
clauses.note: No comparison of characters across texts/cultures occurs.

clauses.clause: Use knowledge of narrative techniques to create texts that share real or imagined experiences and events with a sense of closure.
clauses.note: Students do not write or create narratives in this lesson.

verdicts.evidence:
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
"When the author wrote about what the sun sees, was she writing about daytime or nighttime?" (daytime)
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
"What did the sun "see" animals and people doing during the daytime?" (busy children, crowded streets, animals in the barn)
verdicts.rationale: Students identify elements like time of day (setting) and actions/events in a literary text, but they do not analyze plot, character traits, compare characters, or produce narrative writing. [REJECTED: evidence missing or not found in lesson raw text]
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote NOT found in lesson raw text (possible fabrication)

verdicts.evidence:
Invite students to begin the Sorting protocol.
As students circulate and share, prompt them to explain the categories they chose by asking: 'Can you explain what is the same about the pictures in this categories?' ... Tell students that as they watch the videos, they should look carefully to see what they notice and observe about the sky, the sun, the moon, and what animals and people are doing during the daytime and during the nighttime. Tell students they should also think about the questions they have as they watch the videos.
